destination_record.name: Himachal Pradesh
destination_record.tagline: Pine forests, snow peaks and river valleys, from colonial Shimla to adventure in Manali, Solang Valley and the Atal Tunnel.
destination_record.places: Shimla, Kufri, Manali, Solang Valley, Atal Tunnel, Sissu, Kullu, Naggar, Kasol, Manikaran, Dharamshala, McLeod Ganj. Spiti Valley can be planned separately on request.

on.places: Shimla, Kufri, Manali, Solang Valley, Kullu, Kasol, McLeod Ganj
on.activities: Pleasant weather for sightseeing, paragliding at Solang, river rafting on the Beas, walks in the Parvati valley and day trips through the Atal Tunnel to Sissu. Snow still lies at higher places in March. Rohtang Pass opens in late spring or early summer, subject to snow clearing and permit limits. May and June are the busiest and most expensive months.

off.activities: Monsoon season, with heavy rain, landslides and road blockages on the mountain highways. Views are often hidden by cloud and river rafting is suspended. Hotel rates are lower, but journeys can be delayed, so keep your plans flexible and avoid tight onward connections.

mid.places: Manali, Solang Valley, Shimla, Kufri, Kullu, McLeod Ganj
mid.activities: September and October bring clear mountain views, apple orchards and the Kullu Dussehra festival. From December to February it is cold, with snow around Manali, Solang Valley, Shimla and Kufri for snow play and skiing. Some high roads close after heavy snowfall and Rohtang Pass stays shut.

profile.overview:
Himachal Pradesh is the Himalayan state that most Indian families picture when they think of the mountains: deodar and pine forests, snow peaks above the Beas and Parvati rivers, orchards, monasteries and hill towns with a colonial past. Shimla gives you the Ridge, Mall Road and the old railway, Manali and Solang Valley bring snow and adventure, Kasol has riverside cafes in the Parvati valley, and McLeod Ganj is the home of the Tibetan community in exile.

It is easy to reach from Chandigarh, Delhi and the Kullu-Manali airport, and a week is enough for a satisfying circuit. The Atal Tunnel now opens the Lahaul valley to a day trip from Manali. Tell us your dates, group size and budget, and we will build the itinerary around you.

facts.languages: Hindi, Pahari dialects, Punjabi, English in tourist areas
facts.climate: Hill climate: about 15 to 30°C in summer, near or below freezing with snow from December to February at higher places, and heavy rain in July and August
facts.flight_time: Fly to Chandigarh (about 1 hr from Delhi; from Chennai usually one-stop via Delhi) or Kullu-Manali airport; Delhi to Manali by overnight Volvo takes about 12 to 14 hr

reasons.title: Snow and mountain scenery
reasons.text: Manali, Solang Valley and Kufri have snow in winter, and the Dhauladhar and Pir Panjal ranges frame the views for much of the year.

reasons.title: A complete hill-station circuit
reasons.text: Shimla, Kullu, Manali and Dharamshala each have a different character, so one trip can mix heritage, adventure and quiet time.

reasons.title: Adventure for every age
reasons.text: Paragliding, river rafting, ropeway rides and gentle valley walks suit couples, friends and families alike.

reasons.title: Easy to reach from every metro
reasons.text: Chandigarh and Kullu-Manali have flights, and overnight Volvo buses run from Delhi, so you need only a few days of leave.

reasons.title: Culture and calm
reasons.text: Temples, Buddhist monasteries and gurudwaras sit beside apple orchards and village homestays.

attractions.title: The Ridge and Mall Road, Shimla
attractions.text: The old summer capital of British India, with Christ Church, colonial buildings and a lively pedestrian promenade.

attractions.title: Kalka-Shimla railway
attractions.text: A narrow-gauge mountain railway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, winding through tunnels and bridges.

attractions.title: Hadimba Devi Temple, Manali
attractions.text: A wooden pagoda-style temple in a cedar forest, among the best-known sights of the town.

attractions.title: Solang Valley
attractions.text: A wide meadow valley near Manali for snow play, skiing in winter, paragliding and ropeway rides.

attractions.title: Atal Tunnel and Sissu
attractions.text: A highway tunnel about 9 km long under the Rohtang range that opens the green Lahaul valley as a day trip from Manali.

attractions.title: Kullu Valley and Naggar
attractions.text: The Beas river valley with the Raghunath Temple in Kullu, and Naggar's old castle and Roerich art gallery.

attractions.title: Kasol and Manikaran, Parvati valley
attractions.text: Pine-covered riverside villages, with hot springs and a well-known gurudwara at Manikaran.

attractions.title: McLeod Ganj and Dharamshala
attractions.text: The Tsuglagkhang temple complex, home of the Dalai Lama, with Tibetan cafes, monasteries and Bhagsu waterfall.

experiences.title: Paragliding at Solang Valley
experiences.text: A tandem flight over the valley with a trained pilot, available in suitable weather.

experiences.title: Snow play and skiing
experiences.text: From December to February, Solang Valley and the slopes around Manali and Kufri turn white.

experiences.title: Drive through the Atal Tunnel
experiences.text: Go from the Manali side to the Lahaul valley in minutes, with views of snow peaks and the waterfall at Sissu.

experiences.title: River rafting on the Beas
experiences.text: A seasonal ride on the rapids near Kullu, usually in spring and early summer, supervised by trained guides.

experiences.title: Tibetan culture in McLeod Ganj
experiences.text: Visit monasteries, taste momos and browse shops selling prayer flags and handicrafts.

experiences.title: Riverside walks in the Parvati valley
experiences.text: Easy village paths near Kasol and Chalal, with cafes and views of the Parvati river.

food.title: Himachali dham
food.text: A festive meal served on leaf plates, with dal, rajma, madra and rice, traditionally cooked by specialist chefs.

food.title: Siddu
food.text: A steamed wheat bread, often stuffed with poppy seeds or walnuts, eaten with ghee or dal.

food.title: Trout fish
food.text: Fresh river trout is a speciality of the Kullu and Manali area.

food.title: Tibetan momos and thukpa
food.text: Steamed dumplings and noodle soup, best sampled in McLeod Ganj and Manali.

food.title: Vegetarian and Jain meals
food.text: Most hotels cook simple vegetarian food, and we can arrange Jain meals on request in the main towns.

tips.title: Allow for slow mountain roads
tips.text: Shimla to Manali takes 7 to 8 hours and Chandigarh to Manali 8 to 9 hours, so avoid tight connections on travel days.

tips.title: Pack layers in every season
tips.text: Evenings are cool even in summer, and Solang Valley and the Atal Tunnel are much colder than Manali town.

tips.title: Respect altitude sickness
tips.text: Sissu and the Atal Tunnel are above 3,000 m and Rohtang Pass is near 4,000 m. Go slowly, drink water and come down if you feel unwell.

tips.title: Watch the monsoon and winter roads
tips.text: Landslides in July and August and heavy snow from December can close roads, including Rohtang Pass and parts of the Lahaul side.

tips.title: Carry some cash
tips.text: Mobile networks and ATMs are patchy in Kasol, Sissu and smaller villages, so keep notes for cafes and taxis.

tips.title: Dress modestly at holy places
tips.text: Cover your head at gurudwaras such as Manikaran, and follow the rules at temples and Buddhist monasteries.

travel_info.visa: Indian citizens need no visa for Himachal Pradesh, but every adult must carry a valid government photo ID such as an Aadhaar card, passport, driving licence or voter ID for hotel check-in. Rohtang Pass needs a vehicle permit that is issued within daily limits, and rules for other high-altitude places can change. We arrange permits and confirm the current rules at booking.
travel_info.health: No compulsory vaccinations. Manali is at about 2,050 m and Solang Valley at about 2,500 m, while Sissu and the Atal Tunnel are above 3,000 m and Rohtang Pass is close to 4,000 m. Headache, nausea or breathlessness can be signs of altitude sickness, so go slowly, drink water, avoid alcohol and descend if symptoms worsen. Roads are full of curves, so carry travel-sickness tablets and your regular medicines.
travel_info.money: Carry some cash, as ATMs and UPI networks are patchy in Kasol, Sissu and Lahaul. Cards and UPI work in Shimla, Manali and McLeod Ganj hotels, shops and larger restaurants. Keep small notes for taxis, cafes and tips.

faqs.q: How many days do I need for Himachal Pradesh?
faqs.a: Five to six nights cover Shimla and Manali or Manali with Kasol. Add two nights for Dharamshala and McLeod Ganj, and allow extra travel time because the roads are slow.

faqs.q: When is the best time to visit?
faqs.a: March to June is pleasant and best for sightseeing and adventure. September to November has clear views, and December to February is for snow. July and August are monsoon months with a risk of landslides.

faqs.q: Can we see snow in Manali?
faqs.a: Snow usually falls from December to February in Manali, Solang Valley and Kufri. In other months, the Atal Tunnel and the Lahaul side can still show snow-covered peaks.

faqs.q: Is Rohtang Pass included in your itineraries?
faqs.a: No. Rohtang Pass opens only in summer, needs a vehicle permit within daily limits and can close at short notice, so we visit the Lahaul valley through the Atal Tunnel instead. Ask us if you want Rohtang added in season.
Spiti is a high-altitude trip of its own, with Kaza at around 3,800 m and roads that close with snow. It needs a longer itinerary, so tell us your dates and we will plan it separately.

faqs.q: How do we reach Himachal from Chennai?
faqs.a: Fly to Chandigarh, usually with a stop in Delhi, then drive to Shimla or Manali. You can also fly to Delhi and take an overnight Volvo to Manali, or fly into Kullu-Manali airport.

group_trips.title: McLeod Ganj, Manali and Atal Tunnel Group Trip
group_trips.summary: Seven days in the Himalayan foothills, from the Dalai Lama's temple in McLeod Ganj to Hadimba temple, Solang Valley and the Atal Tunnel near Manali, travelling in a small group.
group_trips.overview:
This group trip links two of Himachal's best-loved hill destinations over six nights: two in McLeod Ganj and four in Manali. In McLeod Ganj you visit the Tsuglagkhang temple complex, home of the Dalai Lama, walk to Bhagsu waterfall and enjoy the Tibetan cafes. A long but scenic drive through the Kangra and Kullu valleys then takes you to Manali.

In Manali you see Hadimba Devi Temple and Old Manali, spend a day at Solang Valley and drive through the Atal Tunnel to Sissu in the Lahaul valley. A fourth day takes in Kullu and Naggar. A trip captain travels with the group, and vegetarian and Jain meal options are available on request.

The drives are long on two days, so the pace on the other days is easy, which suits families, friends and senior parents.

honeymoon_trips.title: Shimla and Manali Honeymoon: Pine Forests, Snow Peaks and Candlelit Evenings
honeymoon_trips.summary: Five unhurried nights for two in Shimla and Manali, with a flower welcome, a private day to Solang Valley and the Atal Tunnel, a couples spa session and a candlelight dinner.
honeymoon_trips.overview:
This private honeymoon pairs two of Himachal's best-loved hill stations: two nights in Shimla and three in Manali. You travel by private car, start most mornings late and keep the afternoons and evenings for each other.

Shimla brings colonial streets, the Ridge and a drive to Kufri for mountain views. A scenic day on the road through the Kullu valley takes you to Manali, where you see Hadimba Devi Temple, then spend a private day at Solang Valley and the Atal Tunnel with a ropeway ride.

Expect a flower welcome or room decoration on arrival, a couples spa session and a candlelight dinner, all subject to availability. Please tell us your wedding date at booking.

custom_trips.title: Shimla, Kullu and Manali Classic Himachal Circuit
custom_trips.summary: Six nights across the classic Himachal circuit, from Shimla's colonial Ridge to Hadimba temple, Solang Valley, the Atal Tunnel and the Kullu valley, arranged as a private holiday.
custom_trips.overview:
This private holiday covers the classic Himachal circuit in six nights: two in Shimla and four in Manali. You see the Ridge, Christ Church and Kufri in Shimla, then drive through the Kullu valley to Manali.

In Manali you visit Hadimba Devi Temple and Old Manali, spend a day at Solang Valley and the Atal Tunnel, and take a day trip to Kullu and Naggar. Dates, hotels and pace can be adjusted to suit your group, so ask us for a quote.

custom_trips.summary: Five nights of river valleys and mountains, with the Parvati valley around Kasol and Manikaran, adventure at Solang Valley and a drive through the Atal Tunnel, arranged on request.
custom_trips.overview:

In Manali you spend a day at Solang Valley, drive through the Atal Tunnel to Sissu and keep a day free for optional river rafting on the Beas, Naggar and Old Manali. Adventure activities are optional, seasonal and paid locally, so tell us your dates and interests and we will send a quote.
